content.title: About
content.content: Beef strip steak (also known as New York strip) is a boneless cut from the short loin of the cow. It is prized for its tender texture, moderate marbling, and rich beef flavor. Commonly grilled, pan‑seared, or oven‑roasted, it is best served at medium doneness to retain juiciness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Strip steak is one of the most valuable beef cuts because of its tenderness.
The name “strip” comes from the long, strip‑like shape of the muscle.
In the United States it is often marketed as “New York Strip”.
Marbling (intramuscular fat) greatly influences flavor and juiciness.
Boneless cuts cook faster and are easier to slice than bone‑in versions.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Strip steak provides about 26 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron and zinc
items.content: Beef supplies highly bioavailable heme iron and zinc, essential for immune function and metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: It contains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which help maintain nerve health and energy production.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: Moderate amounts of intramuscular fat deliver monounsaturated omega‑9 fatty acids that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: The combination of protein and fat promotes prolonged feelings of fullness.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive intake may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked beef can harbor pathogens such as E. coli.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Beef is high in purines, which can exacerbate gout symptoms.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Season the strip steak with salt and pepper, let it reach room temperature, then sear on high heat to the desired doneness (rare, medium, well‑done). Serve with vegetables, potatoes, or a light sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh steak refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for 3‑5 days, tightly wrapped. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Thaw in the refrigerator before cooking.
